newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- APRIL 16.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Greece has agreed to a compromise on the participation of Turkey in EU bodies, saying that Turkey can contribute to decisions on military activities undertaken by the Western European Union if this requires the participation of NATO ifnrastructure. The announcement was made by Brussels.

--As part of efforts to trim the state's expenditures, the environment, town planning and public works ministry is working on a new bill that will establish a state-run insurance company that will handle compensation in event of an earthquake. The new body foresees, according to reports, premiums of 10,000 drachmas per annum for each building and compensation of up to 120,000 drachmas per sq.m.

--The OECD and International Monetary Fund (IMF) are adjusting their policies on social insurance systems and concentrating on the problem in Greece. OECD will soon reveal a special study on the issue while an IMF delegation is due in Athens on May 2 for talks on the matter.
--Business in Bulgaria was on the menu of a working luncheon Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos held yesterday for leading Greek entrepreneurs and visiting Bulgarian Foreign Minister Stoyan Stalev.

--The Papandreou-Liani brawl continues in the wake of Papandreou's children filing suit to reclaim the house sold by the late founder and president of ruling PASOK. Now, the present owner of the house is suing Papandreou's widow Dimitra for compensation.
--Radical changes in the pipeline for the social security system - such as an increase in the retirement age and a ceiling on lump sum payments - will go into effect as of January 1, 1998.
--Greece will participate in tomorrow's exercise on dealing with a nuclear accident.
--The government is making unilateral concessions to Ankara, allowing Turkey a say in WEU decisions and opening the market, to the cost of Greek farmers.
--It took nine hours for a 62-year-old heart patient to be found a bed in intensive care at Athens Red Cross Hospital.
--The Interior Ministry's new bill has changed the code of conduct for civil servants for the first time in 46 years.
--Fishermen netted a 3.5-metre shark in waters off the island of Kea, near the Attica coast. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
